strengths: Strong and consistent experimental results across three benchmarks with significant BD-rate improvements (15.91%-21.34% over VTM-21.0)
Well-motivated problem identification: articulates specific limitations of vanilla Mamba (long-range decay, content-agnostic scanning, strict causality) for 2D image processing
Favorable complexity profile: achieves SOTA performance while maintaining linear complexity, with 36% fewer FLOPs and 43% less memory than comparable methods
Comprehensive evaluation with multiple metrics (PSNR, MS-SSIM, BD-rate), ablation studies clearly showing individual component contributions (CTA: 1.7-2.2%, GPP: 0.7-1.2%)
Effective visualizations including Effective Receptive Field (ERF) and semantic clustering results demonstrating the method's ability to capture global dependencies
Clear presentation with logical structure, detailed experimental setup, and reproducibility information enabling result verification
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: combines relatively straightforward applications of standard techniques (K-means clustering and learnable prompts adapted from Guo et al. 2024a) without significant innovation
Missing critical design choice analysis: no ablation studies or justification for key hyperparameters (e.g., why K=64 clusters? How sensitive is performance to this choice?)

Incomplete statistical validation: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-run experiments despite results being empirically driven; MambaIC comparison based on reproduction rather than official implementation

Insufficient mechanism analysis: lacks formal theoretical justification for why scanning content-similar tokens sequentially improves compression; prompt dictionary's role in 'relaxing causality' is only minor modification to output matrix
Limited experimental scope: clustering visualization shown for only 3 images in one stage; no analysis of performance variation across different image types or content characteristics
Reproducibility gaps: code only promised after acceptance; inference-time clustering procedure, cluster center maintenance during deployment, and token reordering determinism not clearly specified
